parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has one file, src/application/services.ts, and it covers one concern: application use cases for the project, task and user aggregates. UserService and TaskManagementService both depend on domain repository interfaces and the shared IdGenerator port. CreateTaskInput and ListTasksInput are DTOs for the use cases. The not-found checks live once, in the private helpers requireProject, requireTask and requireUser, and state changes go through domain functions (createTask, assignTask, markTaskDone, createProject, createUser) rather than editing tasks directly. There are minor concerns. listTasks checks status with isTaskStatus, but addTask casts it unchecked ('input.status as TaskStatus | undefined'), which probably relies on createTask checking it in the domain. The listTasks error message hardcodes the status list 'todo, in progress, done', copying text from the domain. addTask also does its own due-date type check. These are small inconsistencies that I can't fully check without the domain source. They don't amount to a split concern, a clearly duplicated rule, or a bypass of the module's own abstractions.
